Michael Carter-Williams was born on October 10, 1991.
Michael Carter-Williams is an American professional basketball player.
Michael Carter-Williams last played for the Capitanes de Ciudad de México of the NBA G League.
Michael Carter-Williams was drafted in the first round with the 11th overall pick in the 2013 NBA draft by the Philadelphia 76ers.
Michael Carter-Williams played college basketball for the Syracuse Orange.
Michael Carter-Williams was named NBA Rookie of the Year in 2014.
Michael Carter-Williams has also played for the Milwaukee Bucks, Chicago Bulls, Charlotte Hornets, Houston Rockets, and Orlando Magic.
Carter-Williams attended Hamilton-Wenham Regional High School in Hamilton, Massachusetts as a freshman.
Carter-Williams was 5'9" as a freshman at Hamilton-Wenham Regional High School.
Carter-Williams led his team and conference in scoring with 20 points per game during his freshman year at Hamilton-Wenham Regional High School.
Carter-Williams won a league championship during his freshman year at Hamilton-Wenham Regional High School.
In 2008, Carter-Williams transferred to the boarding school St. Andrew's in Barrington, Rhode Island.
Carter-Williams lived in a dormitory during his final three years of high school at St. Andrew's.
Carter-Williams was a starter for St. Andrew's for three years.
During his three years as a starter at St. Andrew's, Carter-Williams averaged 25.4 points per game.
As a senior at St. Andrew's, Carter-Williams averaged 23.2 points per game.
As a senior at St. Andrew's, Carter-Williams averaged 8.3 rebounds and 5.5 assists per game.
Carter-Williams had a subdued freshman season at Syracuse in 2011–12.
In the 2011–12 season, Carter-Williams played behind Scoop Jardine, Brandon Triche, and Dion Waiters.
During his freshman year at Syracuse, Carter-Williams did not play in games and received sporadic minutes in others.
Carter-Williams finished his freshman season with averages of 2.7 points, 2.1 rebounds, and 10.3 minutes in 26 total games (no starts).
During the 2012 offseason, Carter-Williams worked on his game to get stronger.
During the 2012 offseason, Carter-Williams did shooting drills every morning.
During the 2012 offseason, Carter-Williams improved his nutrition.
Carter-Williams emerged as a breakout star for Syracuse and one of the best point guards in the nation during the 2012–13 season.
In the 2012–13 season, Carter-Williams started his first game for Syracuse in the season opener.
During the 2012–13 season, Carter-Williams kept his starting role for the entire season.
Carter-Williams finished his sophomore season with averages of 11.9 points per game, 5.0 rebounds per game, 7.3 assists per game, and 2.7 steals per game in 35.2 minutes per game.
On March 28, 2013, Carter-Williams scored a career-high 24 points as he led Syracuse past the No. 1 seed Indiana Hoosiers 61–50 in the NCAA's East Region semi-finals.
At the conclusion of the 2012–13 season, Carter-Williams earned Associated Press honorable mention All-American honors.
At the conclusion of the 2012–13 season, Carter-Williams also earned second-team All-Big East honors.
On April 10, 2013, Carter-Williams declared for the NBA draft, forgoing his final two years of college eligibility.
Carter-Williams was selected 11th overall in the 2013 NBA draft by the Philadelphia 76ers.
In the 2013–14 season, Carter-Williams was named the Player of the Week in only his first week in the NBA.

On October 30, 2013, in his NBA debut, Carter-Williams recorded 22 points, 12 assists, 7 rebounds, and 9 steals (the most steals ever made by a rookie on debut) in a 114–110 win over the defending champion Miami Heat.
Less than a week later, Carter-Williams had a 26-point, 10 assist performance in a 107–104 win over the Chicago Bulls.
Carter-Williams was named the Eastern Conference Rookie of the Month for games played in October and November 2013.
During January 2014, Carter-Williams led all rookies in scoring (16.5 ppg).
During January 2014, Carter-Williams ranked second in rebounding (5.6 rpg), assists (5.6 apg) and minutes (33.3 mpg).
On December 3, 2013, Carter-Williams recorded his first triple-double with 27 points, 12 rebounds, and 10 assists in 47 minutes in a 126–125 double-overtime victory over the Orlando Magic.
Carter-Williams participated in the BBVA Rising Stars Challenge and the Taco Bell Skills Challenge during February.
On March 10, 2014, Carter-Williams recorded his second career triple-double with 23 points, 10 assists, and 13 rebounds in a 123–110 loss to the New York Knicks.
Carter-Williams became the first rookie in 76ers franchise history to record two triple doubles in a season.
On April 14, 2014, Carter-Williams recorded 21 points and a career high 14 rebounds.
The 14 rebounds were the most recorded by a point guard in the 2013–14 NBA season.
Carter-Williams finished his rookie season with averages of 16.7 ppg, 6.2 rpg, and 6.3 apg.
At the time, Carter-Williams was one of only three players in NBA history to average 16 points, 6 rebounds and 6 assists in a rookie season.
On May 5, 2014, he was named the 2014 NBA Rookie of the Year.
Carter-Williams underwent shoulder surgery in May 2014.
Carter-Williams subsequently missed the 2014 NBA Summer League and training camp.
Carter-Williams, along with Nerlens Noel, were both officially signed by the 76ers on September 24, 2013.
On November 13, 2014, Carter-Williams made his season debut against the Dallas Mavericks.
In 30 minutes off the bench, he recorded a team-high 19 points as well as 8 rebounds and 5 assists in a 123–70 loss.
On November 29, 2014, Carter-Williams recorded his third career triple-double with 18 points, 10 rebounds, and a career high 16 assists.
On December 13, 2014, he recorded his fourth career triple-double with 16 points, 11 rebounds, and 11 assists.
On February 19, 2015, Carter-Williams was traded to the Milwaukee Bucks in a three-team deal involving the Phoenix Suns.
Carter-Williams made his debut for the Bucks on February 25, recording 7 points and 8 assists as a starter in a 104–88 win over his former team the Philadelphia 76ers.
On April 8, 2015, Carter-Williams scored a season-high 30 points in a loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers.
Five days later, he matched his season-high with 30 points in his first game back in Philadelphia since being traded to lead the Bucks to a 107–97 win over the 76ers.
On October 17, 2016, Carter-Williams was traded to the Chicago Bulls in exchange for Tony Snell.
Carter-Williams made his debut for the Bulls on October 27, 2016, recording five points, six rebounds and three assists off the bench in a 105–99 win over the Boston Celtics.
On November 1, 2016, Carter-Williams was ruled out for four to six weeks after he sustained a bone bruise with no ligament damage to his knee.
Carter-Williams returned to the Bulls lineup on December 26, 2016, and finished with one point (0-for-5 from the field) in 19 minutes against the Indiana Pacers.
On July 7, 2017, Carter-Williams signed with the Charlotte Hornets.
On March 9, 2018, he was ruled out for the rest of the season with a posterior labral tear in his left shoulder.
On July 6, 2018, Carter-Williams signed with the Houston Rockets.
On December 19, 2018, in a 136–118 win over the Washington Wizards, Carter-Williams hit a 3-pointer late in the fourth quarter to give the Rockets an NBA-record 26th 3-pointer for the game.
On March 15, 2019, Carter-Williams signed a 10-day contract with the Orlando Magic.
Carter-Williams signed a second 10-day contract on March 25.
That same day, he recorded a season-high 15 points in a 119–98 win over his former team, the Philadelphia 76ers.
On April 4, 2019, the Magic signed Carter-Williams for the remainder of the season.
On July 10, 2019, Carter-Williams re-signed with the Magic on a one-year contract.
On November 24, 2020, Carter-Williams re-signed with the Magic on a 2-year, $6.6 million contract.
On August 23, 2021, Carter-Williams underwent surgery on his left ankle and was ruled out for the start of the 2021–22 season.
On February 10, 2022, he was waived without playing a game during the season for the Magic.
On February 26, 2023, Carter-Williams re-signed with the Magic.
On October 30, 2023, Carter-Williams signed with the Capitanes de Ciudad de México of the NBA G League.
On December 26, 2023, Carter-Williams parted ways with Capitanes for personal reasons.
Carter-Williams formed NFT company DeFi Crypto Connections with partners Brooks Brown and Austin Greishober in 2021.
Carter-Williams is involved with youth athletics organization MCW Starz, which was founded by his mother Mandy and step-father Zach.
Carter-Williams is also involved with a sports trading card project he founded with MLB prospect Blaze Jordan.
Michael Carter-Williams is the son of Earl Williams and Mandy Zegarowski (née Carter) and step-son of Zach Zegarowski and Rosa Williams.
Michael Carter-Williams has a younger sister, Masey, and three younger brothers: Marcus, Max, and Adrian.
